Adult hydrocephalus.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Mr. Watson is an 86-year-old male who returns in follow-up for adult hydrocephalus. This is his first visit since undergoing shunt surgery on August 1st, 2020.

The patient was status post shunt placement on August 1st, 2020, with a Medtronic Strata programmable shunt in the ventricular peritoneal configuration placed at level 2.0.

The patient reports that he has been doing much better since his shunt surgery. He notes that his walking has improved and he is now able to walk to the dining room just fine. However, he still has times where he needs assistance. His bladder control did improve after surgery but has leveled out and he is now wearing diapers.

Regarding his cognitive status, the patient states that he feels better and does not feel lost when talking to someone anymore. His daughter notes that she feels like she can have a normal conversation with him again.

The patient denies any headaches or pain related to the shunt placement. He also denies any abdominal pain.

PAST HISTORY

The patient reports a history of urinary incontinence, adult hydrocephalus, gait impairment, and cognitive impairment.

CURRENT MEDICATIONS AND ALLERGIES

The patient reports no current medications or allergies.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Hypertension.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Amanda Taylor is a 72-year-old female who presents for follow-up for hypertension. Her history includes significant alcohol use disorder and MI. At her last visit on April 16th, her blood pressure was 130/90. After presenting at 150/100, she was prescribed hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg by mouth once daily, and lisinopril 20 mg by mouth once daily. CMP and CBC were essentially unremarkable.

The patient reports that she has been drinking alcohol 4 to 5 times a week to excess. She denies any tobacco use or substance abuse. She is taking her blood pressure medications as prescribed but only taking half of the lisinopril due to side effects such as lethargy, headaches, and ear fullness. She denies chest tightness or pressure or shortness of breath.

The patient reports that she has been doing blood pressure checks at home and notes that her numbers are generally lower in the morning than in the evening, with readings ranging from 130 to 145/95 to 100 mmHg. However, her numbers tend to improve after sitting for a while or after taking medication in the morning.

She is also taking her hydrochlorothiazide medication as prescribed.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Cardiovascular: Denies chest tightness or pressure or shortness of breath.
• Neurological: Denies tremor.
• Psychiatric: Reports anxiety.

note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Alcohol Use Disorder.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient reports that she has been drinking alcohol 4 to 5 times a week to excess. She denies any tobacco use or substance abuse. She is taking her blood pressure medications as prescribed but only taking half of the lisinopril due to side effects such as lethargy, headaches, and ear fullness.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed the potential benefits of alcohol cessation in terms of improving hypertension control, reducing risk for cardiovascular disease, improving sleep quality, reducing anxiety symptoms, improving overall quality of life, and reducing risk for certain cancers.
- Medical Treatment: We discussed Naltrexone which blocks some of the brain receptors that alcohol stimulates and tricks the brain into thinking it does not need alcohol thereby cutting down on urges for drinking alcohol.
- Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with the recommended medical treatment plan.
- Additional Testing or Procedures: We will schedule a follow-up appointment in week of June 14th which is likely around the time of her second Naltrexone injection.
2. Hypertension.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient reports that she has been drinking alcohol 4 to 5 times a week to excess which may be contributing to her hypertension control issues at this time she is taking lisinopril 10 mg daily and hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg daily which may also be contributing to her hypertension control issues at this time her target BP is 130/140 over 70/80 mmHg.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed the potential benefits of alcohol cessation in terms of improving hypertension control, reducing risk for cardiovascular disease, improving sleep quality, reducing anxiety symptoms, improving overall quality of life, and reducing risk for certain cancers.
- Medical Treatment: Continue current medications as prescribed with close monitoring of blood pressure at home until we see improvement with cessation of alcohol consumption.

Ongoing management of rheumatoid arthritis.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Mr. Tyler Nelson is a 72-year-old male who presents for ongoing management of rheumatoid arthritis. Last time he was seen, he received a steroid injection in his right knee on 03/04/2021. He reports that the injection did not help with his pain and swelling. He states that his knee is still swollen and painful, and the whole leg is getting swollen. He rates his pain level as 3 out of 10, but typically it is around 6 on a normal day. The swelling has been present for approximately 2 months now.

The patient reports that he has tried wearing compression socks to help with the swelling, but it has not been helpful. He notes that he has slowed down a bit due to the pain, but when he sits for a while, he experiences stiffness and difficulty getting up without using a cane to get his bearings. The stiffness improves after a little while, but the initial getting up is very difficult.

The patient reports that he has been taking his Xeljanz XR daily as prescribed and also taking Celebrex 200 mg daily, which he started approximately 2 months ago. He states that Celebrex has been working well until the swelling started again.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports right knee pain and swelling.
Cardiovascular: Denies any chest pain or dyspnea.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

• Musculoskeletal: Examination of the right knee reveals range of motion slightly diminished. There is pitting edema around the knee and ankle with normal capillary refill in the toes. The area appears warm to touch due to inflammation.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Fluid aspiration was performed today in office due to persistent swelling and pain in this area.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Right knee effusion with inflammation.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient presents today for ongoing management of rheumatoid arthritis. Last time he was seen, he received a steroid injection in his right knee on 03/04/2021. He reports that the injection did not help with his pain and swelling. Examination reveals range of motion slightly diminished with pitting edema around the knee and ankle with normal capillary refill in the toes.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed alternative treatments such as reducing salt intake, elevating his legs at night, wearing compression stockings, physical therapy, or surgery consultation if necessary.
- Medical Treatment: We will proceed with fluid aspiration followed by steroid injection today in office due to persistent swelling and pain in this area.
- Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with the recommended medical treatment plan.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Perioral dermatitis, rosacea, including ocular rosacea.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Jacqueline Miller is a 40-year-old female who presents to the clinic today for a follow-up examination. She was previously seen on for perioral dermatitis, rosacea, including ocular rosacea. At that time, she was using doxycycline cream twice daily and MetroCream once daily. She noticed improvement with the doxycycline cream but plateaued when she switched to once daily. She stopped breastfeeding and started taking doxycycline at that time.

The patient denies breastfeeding at this time. She has been using MetroCream and Sulfacetamide wash twice daily. She denies any other lotions or moisturizers.

The patient reports that her symptoms have not improved with the current treatment regimen. She notes that she started taking doxycycline once daily last week and has not seen any improvement in her symptoms.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Skin: Reports perioral dermatitis, rosacea, including ocular rosacea.
Constitutional: Denies fever, chills, weight loss or gain.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Skin: Fitzpatrick skin type IV. There are a few faint erythematous papules on bilateral medial cheeks and some redness around and underneath the nostrils.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Perioral dermatitis, rosacea, including ocular rosacea.
Copy and paste her patient instructions.
I have reviewed the patient's current treatment plan with her today. We discussed alternative treatments for her perioral dermatitis, rosacea, including ocular rosacea. I recommended that she continue using MetroCream twice daily until her rash is resolved. I also recommended that she increase her use of doxycycline to twice daily until her rash is resolved. After the rash is resolved, we will decrease the use of doxycycline to once daily for one week before stopping it altogether.
In addition to these treatments, I recommended that she use Vanicream as a gentle cleanser once a day on her eyelids as needed. If she notices any dryness or irritation with Vanicream, we can try petroleum jelly as an alternative moisturizer.
I advised the patient to avoid any anti-aging products or plant-based products until we discuss them further at our next visit.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Right upper quadrant pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Michael Rodriguez is a 47-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of right upper quadrant pain. The onset of his pain began several weeks ago. He describes the pain as severe and localized to the right side of his abdomen, just below his ribs. The pain is intermittent in nature but when it occurs, it is quite severe. He rates his pain on a scale of 0-10 with an 8 being the worst he has ever experienced. The patient notes that his pain is worse after meals, but also occurs 2 hours after meals. He denies any weight loss or vomiting associated with his symptoms.

The patient reports that he has been managing his type 2 diabetes with diet and exercise since he was diagnosed. He notes that he has lost 25 pounds over the last 3 months and his blood sugar levels have improved. However, he continues to experience right upper quadrant pain.

The patient reports that he has a family history of cholelithiasis as both of his parents have had cholecystectomies.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Constitutional: Denies fevers.
• Digestive: Reports nausea and vomiting associated with right upper quadrant pain.
• Musculoskeletal: Denies lower extremity pain.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

VITALS
• Blood Pressure: 128/88 mmHg.
• Respiratory Rate: 16 breaths per minute.
• Heart Rate: 68 beats per minute.
• Oxygen Saturation: 99% on room air.
• Body Temperature: Afebrile.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Abdominal ultrasound obtained at an outside facility shows multiple gallstones present in the gallbladder with some mild thickening. The common bile duct size is within normal limits at 4.1 mm.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Michael Rodriguez is a 47-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of right upper quadrant pain.

Medical Reasoning:
The patient's abdominal ultrasound shows multiple gallstones present in the gallbladder with some mild thickening. The common bile duct size is within normal limits at 4.1 mm. His symptoms are consistent with mild cholecystitis due to gallstones, which appears to have been present for several weeks based on the onset of symptoms and radiographic findings.
In addition to dietary modifications, which have not provided relief from symptoms, we will proceed with surgical intervention due to failure of conservative management to improve symptoms.
Surgical Treatment Plan:
The patient will undergo a laparoscopic cholecystectomy, which will be performed under general anesthesia in our operating room suite today at [insert time]. We anticipate that this procedure will take approximately one hour to one hour and a half and we will keep him overnight for observation post-operatively as well as monitor him for any complications post-operatively until discharge on day two or three when we expect him to be able to ambulate on solid ground by day one or two post-operatively and follow up in clinic at week one post-operatively when we expect him to be discharged from hospital status at that point.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Right shoulder pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Matthew Allen is a 67-year-old right-hand-dominant male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of right shoulder pain. The onset of his symptoms began approximately 4 days ago when he was playing tackle football. He sustained a fall onto his right shoulder and has been experiencing pain ever since. He denies any numbness or tingling in his fingers, but reports that he is having difficulty lifting anything too heavy. He notes that he is able to perform daily activities without difficulty, but is trying to avoid lifting anything too heavy. His pain is located on the back side of his right shoulder, just proximal to the acromioclavicular joint. He denies any neck problems or other joint problems such as elbow or wrist pain. The patient reports that he has not had any previous orthopedic injuries to his right shoulder.

The patient reports that he has been taking Tylenol for pain relief, which has not provided any relief.

PAST HISTORY

The patient reports that he had an appendectomy 3-4 years ago.

SOCIAL HISTORY

The patient reports that he is right-hand dominant and denies previous orthopedic injuries to his right shoulder.

MEDICATIONS AND ALLERGIES

The patient reports that he takes Tylenol for pain relief.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Cervical Spine: No tenderness to palpation of the cervical spine. Full range of motion on head exam. No ecchymosis or bruising on the neck.
Musculoskeletal: Pain with palpation of the posterior shoulder at the acromioclavicular joint. Decreased abduction and adduction to approximately 90 degrees only. Pain with supination and pronation of the right arm. Palpable radial radial artery pulse.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

X-ray of the right shoulder was performed prior to examination today and revealed an acute acromioclavicular joint fracture.
note.assessment_and_plan:

- Medical Treatment: We have placed him in a sling for comfort at this time. We have also prescribed meloxicam 15 mg once daily for pain management. A CT scan will be ordered for further evaluation of the acromioclavicular joint fracture.
- Additional Testing: CT scan of the right shoulder will be ordered for further evaluation of the acromioclavicular joint fracture.
- Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with the recommended medical treatment plan.

Shortness of breath.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Dennis Brown is a 57-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of shortness of breath. He reports that he has been experiencing shortness of breath for approximately 2 weeks. He states that he wakes up with shortness of breath and when he goes to work, he is again short of breath. He notes that he has been coughing up blood and estimates that he coughs up 3-4 tablespoons per day. He denies any hemoptysis at rest. The patient reports that his blood sugar has been going up and down, with morning levels around 1.5 and postprandial levels over 200. He notes that his blood sugar has been high and low for approximately 1 month.

The patient reports that he has been taking Norvasc but has been taking it less frequently due to low blood pressure.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Respiratory: Denies dyspnea on exertion at rest.
• Cardiovascular: Denies chest pain.
• Gastrointestinal: Denies hematemesis.
• Musculoskeletal: Reports knee pain.

Neck
- Supple without carotid bruits.
Lungs
- Auscultation of Lungs: Bilateral rales and rhonchi on the right side, diminished breath sounds on the right side.

- Auscultation of Heart: Grade 2/6 ejection systolic murmur, unchanged from previous exams, regular rate and rhythm otherwise.
Abdomen
- General Examination: Soft.

- General Examination: No calf tenderness or negative Homan sign.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Shortness of Breath.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient presents today for the evaluation of shortness of breath. His oxygen saturation is 94% in the clinic today, but he reports waking up with shortness of breath and when he goes to work, he is again short of breath. He also reports coughing up blood which is estimated to be approximately 3-4 tablespoons per day. His oxygen saturation is stable at this point in time but we will need to get a chest x-ray as well as a CT scan of his chest as well as some blood work done in order to evaluate why he is having these symptoms.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed treatment options with the patient today including obtaining a chest x-ray, CT scan, and blood work in order to evaluate why he is having these symptoms.
- Medical Treatment: We will refer him to the emergency department for further testing including a chest x-ray, CT scan, and blood work as well as start him on antibiotics pending results from his CT scan and blood work.
2. Diabetes Mellitus Type 2.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient presents today for the evaluation of diabetes mellitus type 2. His hemoglobin A1c was elevated last time we saw him at 7%. He reports that his blood sugar has been going up and down with morning levels around 1.5 and postprandial levels over 200 which indicates poor glucose control at this point in time. We discussed treatment options with the patient today including increasing his dose of metformin from 500 mg twice daily to 750 mg twice daily until we get him over this episode with shortness of breath at which point we will recheck his hemoglobin A1c level.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Right elbow pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Teresa Sullivan is a 33-year-old female who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of right elbow pain. The onset of her pain began 4 days ago. She reports that her elbow hurts on the inside and radiates down her arm. She denies any history of trauma to the elbow. The patient has been doing pottery and baking, which she states has been causing her pain. She reports that she has been taking ibuprofen, but it is not helping. The patient states that she is having trouble sleeping due to her pain.

The patient reports that she has a history of hypertension and diabetes type 2. She notes that her blood pressure has been in the 110s to 130s range and blood sugar levels have been from 150 to 170 mg/dL.

PAST HISTORY

History of hypertension.
History of diabetes type 2.

MEDICATIONS

Lisinopril 10 mg daily.
Metformin 500 mg twice daily.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

• Respiratory: Normal respiratory rate, oxygen saturation is 100% on room air, no wheezes or rales bilaterally.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

X-ray of the right elbow reveals no evidence of fracture or bony abnormality.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Right elbow pain.
• Medical Reasoning: The patient's x-ray reveals no evidence of fracture or bony abnormality, which supports the diagnosis of medial epicondylitis.
• Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed with the patient that rest, ice, elevation, compression, and bracing may help alleviate symptoms. We also discussed dietary modifications with regards to reducing sugar intake and increasing protein consumption.
• Medical Treatment: We ordered a sling for the right arm for use while awake. We also ordered ice for 20 minutes, three times a day. We prescribed ibuprofen in doses of six hundred milligrams every six hours with food for one week. We advised the patient to discontinue pottery for two weeks to allow her arm time to heal.
2. Diabetes Type 2.
• Medical Reasoning: Her blood sugar levels have been elevated at times due to inconsistent medication adherence and high carbohydrate intake.
• Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed with the patient that dietary modifications such as reducing sugar intake and increasing protein consumption can help improve blood sugar control. We also recommended referral to diabetic counseling for additional guidance on managing diabetes.
• Medical Treatment: We increased metformin from five hundred milligrams twice daily to one thousand milligrams twice daily. We advised the patient to check her blood sugars every day and follow up with me in two weeks.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Right knee pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Mr. Gregory Price is a 68-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of right knee pain. The onset of his symptoms began 2.5 weeks ago when he stepped off a curb and turned his right ankle to the outside. He denies any actual fall but states that he thought his ankle was going to be the most painful part of the injury. After the initial ankle soreness resolved, he noticed that his right knee was sore and would click when he walks. He denies any pain with ambulation, but notes that if he stands on one foot for an extended period of time, such as leaning his foot up against the wall, he will feel like his knee is locked and will have to ease into walking again.

The patient reports that he has been taking ibuprofen for pain relief, but notes that it does not impact his symptoms during the day as he works through it. However, at night, it does help him to settle down and sleep better.

The patient states that his knee is fine when it is elevated and flat on the floor with his foot up, but will hurt when he rests it on his heel. He denies any pain with rest or ambulation when sitting down.

He reports that he is able to perform a full squat without any pain or clicking, but notes that this is when he feels the most clicking in his knee.

The patient denies any numbness or tingling in his foot at all.

He reports that he has broken his 2nd toe on his right foot 3 times over the last 10 years and notes that this is just an annoyance for him.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports right knee pain.
Neurological: Denies numbness or tingling in the right foot.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Musculoskeletal Examination of Right Knee:
- Palpation: There is slight edema over the lateral aspect of the knee. There is no pain with palpation of the lateral aspect of the right knee. There is a positive varus test bilaterally. Full range of motion bilaterally without evidence of joint effusion.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

X-ray examination reveals no acute fracture or bony abnormality.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Mr. Gregory Price is a 68-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for evaluation of right knee pain.
After reviewing all examination findings today, I believe that Mr. Price has sustained a lateral collateral ligament strain based on examination findings today.
This type of injury can typically be treated conservatively with ice, anti-inflammatory medication and physical therapy to strengthen surrounding muscles which will help prevent future injuries.
I have prescribed meloxicam 15 mg once daily for anti-inflammatory effects and referred him to physical therapy for further strengthening exercises around this area if needed at this point in time I do not think we will need to refer him for surgery at this point in time however if symptoms do not improve after starting treatment we may need to consider an MRI at that point in time.

Right heel pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Dennis Martin is a 46-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of right heel pain. The onset of his symptoms began 10 days ago. He reports that his pain is located in the posterior aspect of his heel, radiating proximally into the calf. His pain is aggravated by working out and when he first gets up in the morning. He notes that he runs 10 kilometers in the morning, bikes for 45 minutes to an hour at lunchtime, and swims for 30 minutes to an hour in the evening. He trains 5 days per week and alternates between a long run and a long bike ride on weekends. He does not stretch at all.

The patient reports that his pain typically begins after he has been walking around for about 10-15 minutes, but if he sits down for any extended period of time and then tries to get back up, it becomes sore again. He also notes that after a lot of activity, his pain will get sore too.

PAST HISTORY

The patient reports that he is currently training for a triathlon.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

MSK Examination: Examination of the lower extremities reveals no left leg pain. The patient's right leg is tender to palpation over the Achilles tendon bilaterally but more so on the right side. The patient's right foot and ankle are tender to palpation with plantarflexion and dorsiflexion of the foot. The patient's left calf is not tender to palpation.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Dennis Martin is a 46-year-old male who presents today for the evaluation of right heel pain.

Medical Reasoning: The patient's symptoms are consistent with Achilles tendinitis due to overuse.
Patient Education and Counseling: I have discussed with him what we discussed today in terms of his current training regimen and how it may be contributing to his symptoms.
Additional Testing: No additional testing was performed today.
Medical Treatment: I have prescribed him ibuprofen or Advil as needed in three tablets every six hours as an anti-inflammatory measure. I have also ordered two physical therapy visits to help him strengthen his lower extremities as well as learn proper stretching techniques before starting these activities again.
Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with the recommended medical treatment plan.
Special Instructions: I would like him to follow up with me within one week to ten days following his first couple physical therapy appointments so we can monitor how he is doing.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Non-healing right foot ulcer.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Christina Cooper is a 77-year-old female who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of a non-healing right foot ulcer. The patient reports that she has had this ulcer for approximately 1 year. She denies any trauma to the foot, but states that she developed a blister and then picked at it, which became red and infected. She was treated with antibiotics, which seemed to improve her symptoms initially, but they have not resolved. The patient reports that she has noticed an increase in drainage from the ulcer and is experiencing fatigue.

The patient reports that her diabetes is well-controlled at this time, but her last hemoglobin A1c was 10. She notes that she has been eating out and not following her doctor's recommendations regarding diet.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Constitutional: Denies fever, chills.
• Musculoskeletal: Denies pain in the right foot.
• Neurological: Reports decreased sensation in the right foot.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

• General Examination: Vital signs are within normal limits today.
• Neurological Examination: Examination of the right foot reveals decreased sensation over the plantar aspect of the lateral aspect of the foot. There is a 1.2 cm x 2 cm circular wound on the dorsal aspect of the lateral right foot proximal to the 5th metatarsal joint. There is yellow slough present with minimal granulation tissue. There is no surrounding erythema or cellulitis and there is no evidence of fluid collection or necrosis. There is no odor and I do not appreciate any bony exposure.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

X-ray of right foot prior to today's visit shows no evidence of osteomyelitis.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Christina Cooper is a 77-year-old female who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of a non-healing right foot ulcer.

Medical Reasoning: The patient's current symptoms are consistent with diabetic neuropathy and non-healing diabetic foot ulcer due to poor wound care and inadequate footwear. Her last hemoglobin A1c was elevated at 10, indicating poorly controlled diabetes mellitus type 2.
Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed dietary modifications with regards to her diabetes mellitus type 2 as well as proper wound care techniques including debridement and dressing changes daily.
Additional Testing: We will order an ankle brachial index (ABI) today to assess for adequate blood flow to her lower extremities.
Medical Treatment: Debridement will be performed in office today followed by prescription for colaganase ointment to be applied once daily with sterile dressing until further improvement is seen. Surgical shoe will be prescribed for ambulation purposes only until further improvement or if debridement does not result in healing.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Concerns about medications.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Jose Thompson is a 75-year-old male who presents for a routine check-up. He reports that he has been doing well on his medications, but he is concerned about the number of medications he is taking. He notes that he has been taking aspirin, Brilinta, fish oil, Crestor, and Metoprolol 50 mg once a day.

The patient reports that he had a heart attack 6 months ago and underwent stent placement at the left anterior descending artery. He notes that he is concerned about the stents and if they will need to be replaced. He denies any chest pain or shortness of breath.

The patient reports that his hemoglobin A1c was 16, which is higher than his target level of 6. He notes that his glucose levels are improving with fasting glucose being approximately 130. The patient reports that he has been watching his sweets but admits to having an affinity for chocolate chip cookies.

The patient reports that he does not know if the heart attack or medication is causing him to feel dizzy when standing up quickly. He denies any other symptoms.

PAST HISTORY

Medical: Heart attack, coronary artery disease, diabetes.
Surgical: Stent placement at the left anterior descending artery.
Social: Lives with his dog, San Francisco 49ers fan.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Neck: No jugular venous distention or carotid bruits.
Cardiovascular: Slight grade 3/6 systolic ejection murmur heard at the left base.
Lower extremities: One plus nonpitting edema.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Kidney function was stable with no evidence of contrast-induced kidney injury.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Coronary Artery Disease.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient had a heart attack 6 months ago and underwent stent placement at the left anterior descending artery. We have him on aspirin and Brilinta for life due to this history. His hemoglobin A1c was elevated at last visit but glucose levels are improving with fasting glucose being approximately 130. We have him on Crestor for cholesterol management and Metoprolol for blood pressure control which may be contributing to his edema.
- Patient Education and Counseling: I have discussed cardiac rehab with him today as well as lifestyle modifications such as diet and exercise to help improve his overall health status.
- Medical Treatment: Refill prescriptions for Metoprolol, Crestor, aspirin, and Brilinta as prescribed today in office.
- Additional Testing: No further testing is needed at this time but we will follow up in 3 months if symptoms develop.
2. Stage III Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD).
- Medical Reasoning: The patient has stage III CKD based on creatinine level from last visit which indicates kidney dysfunction due to contrast dye from prior imaging studies. We have advised him to avoid NSAIDs such as Motrin and Advil due to potential renal toxicity.
- Patient Education and Counseling: I have advised him to follow up with Dr. Miller in regards to his CKD status today in office.
- Medical Treatment: Referral sent out today for Dr. Miller for further evaluation of CKD status.
3. Diabetes Mellitus Type II.
- Medical Reasoning: His hemoglobin A1c was elevated at last visit but glucose levels are improving with fasting glucose being approximately 130. We have advised him to follow up with dietitian for dietary education today in office as well as discuss insulin regimen with primary care physician today in office.
- Patient Education and Counseling: I have discussed dietary education with him today in office as well as referred him out to dietitian for further education today in office.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Abdominal pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Barbara White is a 31-year-old female who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of abdominal pain. The onset of her pain began 1 week ago. She reports that she has been drinking a lot of coffee lately, and she suspects that this may have triggered her gastritis. She notes that her pain is located on both sides of her upper abdomen and it increases with exercise. She denies fever with her pain. She also reports nausea and vomiting on and off.

The patient reports that she has been drinking a lot of coffee lately, including venti nitro cold brew from Starbucks. She notes that she has been controlling herself this week and only had one cup of coffee.

The patient denies any recent asthma attacks, but notes that she sometimes forgets to take her Flovent twice daily and albuterol as needed for wheezing. She states that she has not had any asthma attacks lately, so she decided to decrease her medication.

PAST HISTORY

History of diabetes type 2.
History of asthma.
History of gastritis.
Moderately heavy alcohol use.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

• Cardiovascular: Grade 3/6 systolic ejection murmur at the left sternal border unchanged from prior exam.
• Respiratory: Mild end-expiratory wheezes in the bilateral lungs. Otherwise normal respiratory exam with excellent air movement.
• Abdomen: Mild tenderness in the epigastrium without guarding or rebound. No tenderness in the right lower quadrant or right upper quadrant.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Urine pregnancy test negative for pregnancy.
CBC normal.
Comprehensive metabolic panel pending.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Acute gastritis.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient's symptoms are consistent with acute gastritis, likely related to caffeine intake and moderately heavy alcohol use. Her history of diabetes type 2 is also present but does not appear to be contributing to her current symptoms at this time.
- Patient Education and Counseling: I advised the patient to cut back on alcohol consumption to less than 2-3 drinks per week and reduce caffeine intake as well. I also recommended cutting back on spicy foods as well as they may be contributing towards her gastritis symptoms.
- Medical Treatment: I have prescribed Zantac for symptom relief and we will check urinalysis, urine pregnancy test, CBC, comprehensive metabolic panel as well as repeat abdominal exam in 4 weeks to see if there are any other issues present at this time.
2. Diabetes Type 2.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient's blood sugar levels have been under control with metformin 500 mg twice daily but we will increase the dose slightly by adding an additional 500 mg once daily in the morning so we can monitor blood sugar levels more closely at our next visit in 4 weeks.
- Patient Education and Counseling: I advised the patient to continue checking her blood sugar levels when she comes back in for follow up in 4 weeks so we can monitor progress at that time.
- Medical Treatment: Continue metformin 1000 mg once daily in the morning and 500 mg once daily in the evening.

Alexis Gutierrez is a 33-year-old female who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of right hand numbness and tingling. She reports that she experiences pain with typing on the keyboard, but not with mouse use. She notes that her symptoms are constant, and she has tried taking ibuprofen which seems to provide some relief. She denies any nocturnal pain or sleep disturbance.

Ms. Gutierrez works on a keyboard all day and reports that her symptoms have been worsening over time.

note.objective_exam:

note.assessment_and_plan:

1. Carpal tunnel syndrome.
- Medical Reasoning: The clinical findings are consistent with carpal tunnel syndrome. The patient's occupation involves frequent use of a keyboard, which is a common cause of this condition.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed the nature of her condition in detail today, including conservative treatment options such as wrist splinting and physical therapy, as well as surgical intervention if necessary.
- Medical Treatment: We will start with a wrist splint at night to help alleviate her symptoms. I have also ordered an EMG for further testing to confirm the diagnosis. I would like her to increase her ibuprofen dose to 600 mg 4 times daily for pain control.
- Additional Testing: EMG ordered for further testing.
- Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with the recommended medical treatment plan.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Acute on chronic congestive heart failure.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Kevin Davis is an 82-year-old male with past medical history significant for hypertension and stage 3 chronic kidney disease who presents for hospital follow-up after an acute on chronic chf exacerbation. He reports that he has been trying to watch his diet as recommended by the physician, but he noticed that his ankles were swelling. He also states that he was trying to watch his diet, but he really noticed that his ankles were swelling and then one day he got really super short of breath and he even had to call 911. When the paramedics got there they put him on the special mask to breathe when he got to the ER the doctor in the ER said his blood pressure was super high.

The patient denies chest pain since he has been home.

PAST HISTORY

Medical History: Hypertension, Stage 3 chronic kidney disease.

SOCIAL HISTORY

Patient reports being a football fan.

MEDICATIONS

Patient reports taking Bumex 2 mg once daily, Cozaar 100 mg daily, and Norvasc 5 mg once daily.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Neck: No jugular venous distention.
Cardiovascular: Grade 2/6 systolic ejection murmur stable. Lungs are clear bilaterally. No wheezes or rales heard. No gallops or murmurs heard at the apex.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Echocardiogram shows preserved ejection fraction of 55% with abnormal diastolic filling and mild to moderate mitral regurgitation.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Acute on Chronic Congestive Heart Failure.
- Medical Reasoning: This was caused by dietary indiscretion in uncontrolled hypertension.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed dietary modifications and avoiding salty foods such as pizza and chicken wings. I also recommended that we see a nutritionist for further education on healthy eating options.
- Medical Treatment: Continue Bumex 2 mg once daily. Weigh himself every day and call if he gains more than 3 pounds in two days.
- Additional Testing: Repeat labs to monitor kidney function.
2. Hypertension.
- Medical Reasoning: Secondary causes need to be ruled out with renal artery ultrasound.
- Patient Education and Counseling: Continue Cozaar 100 mg daily and Norvasc 5 mg once daily as prescribed by the physician.
- Additional Testing: Order renal artery ultrasound to rule out secondary causes of hypertension.
3. Stage 3 Chronic Kidney Disease.
- Medical Reasoning: Repeat labs are needed to monitor kidney function.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Elevated cholesterol.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Julie Cruz is a 17-year-old non-binary patient who presents for evaluation of newly diagnosed hypercholesterolemia. The patient reports that she was recently screened for cholesterol at her annual checkup and her results were elevated. She denies any history of hypercholesterolemia or other lipid disorders. The patient reports that she enjoys being outside and riding her bike on trails. She states that she tries to eat a clean diet most days, but admits to enjoying chocolate chip cookies. She denies any history of family members with hypercholesterolemia or other lipid disorders, but notes that her grandparents had a cousin who died at the age of 44 from a heart attack. The patient reports that she has been doing well with regards to her growth and development, but states that she has been feeling like she is not a girl and identifies as non-binary.

SOCIAL HISTORY

The patient reports that when she lived with her parents, they smoked. However, the patient currently lives alone and does not smoke.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Cardiovascular: Denies chest pain.
• Endocrine: Denies thyroid problems.
• Gastrointestinal: Denies abdominal pain.
• Musculoskeletal: Reports no issues with growth or development.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

• Cardiovascular: Blood pressure is within normal limits. No murmurs, gallops, or rubs appreciated on auscultation of the heart. Lungs are clear bilaterally to auscultation. No thyromegaly appreciated on examination.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Cholesterol level was elevated at 210.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Elevated cholesterol.
- Medical Reasoning: The American Academy of Pediatrics recommends screening all children between the ages of 9-11 and again between the ages of 17-20 for elevated cholesterol levels due to studies showing a link between high cholesterol and premature heart attacks.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed the importance of dietary changes in reducing cholesterol levels and I recommended that we follow up in 3-6 months after meeting with a nutritionist who can provide guidance on healthy eating habits.
- Medical Treatment: We will order a full cholesterol panel, glucose, complete metabolic panel, thyroid studies, liver panels, and genetic testing to determine if this is familial or secondary in nature.
- Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with the recommended medical treatment plan.

• Cardiovascular: Denies dyspnea on exertion, orthopnea, paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea, chest pain radiating to the arm or jaw.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Bilateral knee pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Sophia Jackson is a 30-year-old female who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of bilateral knee pain. The onset of her symptoms began approximately 6 months ago. She denies any specific event that caused the pain. The patient describes her pain as a deep achy pain located behind her patella. She states that she can hear creaking in her knees when she moves. Her pain is worse with ambulation from a seated position, stair climbing, and watching TV. The patient notes that rest typically helps alleviate her symptoms.

The patient reports that she has tried ice and an ACE bandage in the past for symptom relief. She also takes ibuprofen or Aleve occasionally but tries to avoid taking any medications due to side effects.

The patient is an avid runner and has been running 5-6 miles per day, but she has had to decrease her mileage significantly due to knee pain. She runs on a treadmill during the winter months but prefers running outdoors.

She denies any swelling or redness in her knees. The patient reports that she has never injured her knees before, but she did break her arm in 6th grade.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports bilateral knee pain.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Vitals: Overall vital signs are within normal limits.
Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm with no murmurs.
Musculoskeletal: Examination of the lower extremities reveals normal gait. Strength is 3/5 for abduction of legs bilaterally, and 5/5 for the remainder of lower extremity strength. There is tenderness to palpation of the bilateral retinacular retinaculum. Positive patellar grind test bilaterally. Patient is unable to squat due to pain.
Neurological: Patellar and Achilles reflexes are symmetrical.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS
X-rays of bilateral knees were obtained today and reviewed in office today, which show no fractures or osteoarthritis.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Bilateral patellofemoral pain syndrome.
1) Medical Treatment: Continue taking ibuprofen or anti-inflammatory as needed for symptom relief.
2) Physical Therapy: We will refer you to physical therapy where they will provide you with lower extremity exercises to increase strength, mobility, and correct any incorrect running mechanics that you may have.
3) Activity Modification: We will continue to monitor your progress with each visit while you take it easy from running until we see improvement in your symptoms.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Lumbar back pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Kyle Morales is a 58-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of lumbar back pain. The onset of his pain began 2 weeks ago when he was lifting a box of books. He denies any history of trauma. He describes his pain as achy and sharp, primarily located in his low back. Initially, he denies any radiation down his left leg, but now he is experiencing some left leg pain.

The patient reports that he has tried taking ibuprofen and Tylenol, which sometimes helps with his pain. He denies any loss of bladder or bowel control. He states that he is an Olympic weightlifter and has been inconsistent with his exercise routine lately due to his current back pain. His sedentary job does not seem to be contributing to his current level of activity.

The patient reports that his father has back pain.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports low back pain radiating down the left leg.
Neurological: Denies numbness or tingling, weakness, or loss of sensation.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Vitals are within normal limits.
Respiratory: Respiratory rate is 18 per minute in a relaxed position. Lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm without murmurs, gallops, or rubs.
Musculoskeletal: Examination of the musculoskeletal system reveals midline tenderness at the L4-L5 disk space with right-sided lumbar paravertebral tenderness. Pain with lumbar flexion is present.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

MRI of the lumbar spine reveals disc desiccation and a disc bulge with paracentral disc herniation resulting in moderate right neuroforaminal stenosis.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Lumbar back pain due to a herniated disk with radiculopathy.
1) Medical Treatment: Continue taking ibuprofen and Tylenol as needed for symptom management.
2) Interventional Procedure: Schedule an office spinal injection with a strong NSAID and corticosteroid under fluoroscopy today if desired by the patient.

note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Angela Powell is an 81-year-old female who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of left knee pain. The onset of her pain began 1 week ago when she was running with her 5-year-old niece. She states that she twisted her knee in a “funky way.”

The patient reports that she has been limping since the onset of her symptoms and has not improved.

Examination reveals edema and effusion bilaterally, but more pronounced on the left side. There is moderate range of motion, but pain with flexion and extension. Negative Lachman’s test and negative valgus and varus test.

X-rays of the left knee were obtained today, which are normal, revealing no fractures or bony abnormalities.

Based on the clinical findings today, I believe that she has a medial collateral ligament (MCL) strain.

Treatment plan: I am going to start her on tramadol 50 mg twice daily for pain management. She can take Tylenol as needed for breakthrough pain. I am also going to have her wear a knee immobilizer for the next week to keep the knee from moving so it can heal a little bit and reduce some inflammation that she is seeing here. I also want her to ice it three or four times a day for twenty thirty minutes at a time which should help some swelling as well.
I do not want her to run with her niece for the next three weeks so we can allow time to let allow the knee to heal.
If she feels like it’s getting worse, please feel free to call the office and we can get you in possibly do more imaging such as an MRI to see if it’s anything worse but I don’t think it is.

High blood pressure.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Diane Baker is a 28-year-old female with a past medical history significant for depression and hypertension who presents for emergency room follow-up. She reports that her blood pressure was elevated in the emergency room yesterday. She states that she was walking outside because it was sunny and she felt light-headed, and she started to fall. Her boyfriend caught her, and they went to the emergency room immediately. Her blood pressure was elevated at the emergency room, like 200. She denies having a headache.

She has been experiencing high blood pressure once a week, sometimes for a month, which usually resolves after she starts traveling for work. She states that she is not taking her blood pressure medication when she is traveling because she does not bring her cuff with her. She did purchase a cuff previously as we discussed in the past.

She denies taking her lisinopril medication regularly.

She reports that she has been doing well with depression since starting therapy last year. She has been attending therapy once per week and finds it helpful.

Her support system includes her boyfriend, mom, and brother, who are all very close to her.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Cardiovascular: Denies chest pain or shortness of breath.
• Respiratory: Reports nasal congestion due to seasonal allergies.
note.objective_exam:

• Cardiovascular: Carotid bruits are absent in the neck. Slight 2/6 systolic ejection murmur heard at auscultation of the heart. Clear lungs bilaterally without wheezes or rales. Trace pitting edema present in lower extremities bilaterally.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

ECG stable in comparison to last year.
Echocardiogram from just a few months ago shows slightly leaky heart valve with no treatment options available at this time and stable heart murmur.

- Medical Treatment: We will increase her lisinopril dose to 40 mg once daily today. We will have her check her blood pressures regularly through patient portal and make adjustments as necessary if necessary or add a second agent if needed.

- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed alternative treatment options today but we do not feel that medication is necessary at this time given how well she is doing with therapy currently.

The patient reports that he has been doing repetitive motion with biking daily, which he believes may have caused this.

Musculoskeletal: Reports right knee pain.

Neurological: Denies fatigue or fever.
note.objective_exam:

- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed treatment options for coronary artery disease today.

She reports that she had routine blood work done last week and was told that her blood sugars were high, so she came in to discuss this further. She denies any symptoms such as chest pain, shortness of breath, nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. She has been taking metformin 1000 mg daily and has been increasing her dose. She denies any difficulty urinating or burning when urinating.

She reports that her diet has been great lately and she has been avoiding sugars, watching her weight, and power walking every day. She checks her blood sugars in the morning and fasting blood sugars. Her hemoglobin A1c is elevated at 8.1.

She reports that her high blood pressure has been stable on lisinopril and she is monitoring it at home with a cuff. Her right ACL repair was performed 5 years ago and everything is going well so far. She continues to be physically active with power walking about 30 minutes every day.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Cardiovascular: Denies chest pain, shortness of breath.
• Gastrointestinal: Denies nausea, vomiting, diarrhea.
• Genitourinary: Denies dysuria or burning with urination.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

• Neck: Supple without neck stiffness.
• Respiratory: Clear to auscultation bilaterally without wheezes or rales.
• Cardiovascular: Grade 3/6 systolic ejection murmur at the left sternal border.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Hemoglobin A1c: Elevated at 8.1.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Diabetes Type 2.
- Medical Reasoning: Elevated hemoglobin A1c despite being on metformin 1000 mg daily. We should add Jardiance 10 mg daily to see if we can get the hemoglobin A1c down the next time we see each other.
- Patient Education and Counseling: I want you to follow your diet pretty aggressively to see if we can get that hemoglobin A1c down the next time we see each other.
- Medical Treatment: Start Jardiance 10 mg daily today.
- Additional Testing: Order CBC, CMP, lipid panel today.
2. Hypertension.
- Medical Reasoning: Stable on lisinopril at home with a cuff for monitoring.
- Patient Education and Counseling: Continue monitoring your blood pressure at home with a cuff as instructed previously.
- Medical Treatment: Continue lisinopril as prescribed previously.
3. Right ACL Repair Status.
- Medical Reasoning: Stable with no issues with mobility or pain.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Followup of chronic problems.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Bruce Howard is a 60-year-old male with a past medical history of depression, type 2 diabetes, and hypertension. He presents for followup of his chronic problems.

The patient reports that he has been experiencing anxiety and stress over the past year and a half. He notes that he had a nice holiday but it was a lot of work. He is planning to take a vacation in the new year. The patient reports that he has not been able to continue his morning long walks due to the cold weather and is looking for alternative options.

Regarding his depression, the patient states that he has not been ready to try medication yet. He notes that he has been going for long walks outside every morning during the summer months, which was a nice way to be active and get some sun. However, with the changing seasons, he has not been able to continue this activity and is looking into alternative options. The patient denies any thoughts of harming himself or others.

The patient reports that he got through Halloween okay but did not stick to his diet too much during the Thanksgiving week. He notes that it is a little better now and has been trying to monitor his blood sugar levels more closely.

The patient confirms that he is still taking metformin as prescribed.

Regarding his hypertension, the patient reports that his blood pressure cuff was purchased as recommended by the physician. His blood pressure appears to be well controlled at this time.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Constitutional: Denies weight loss or gain.
• Cardiovascular: Denies chest pain or dyspnea on exertion.
• Gastrointestinal: Denies abdominal pain or hematochezia.
• Musculoskeletal: Denies lower extremity edema.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Follow-up.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Maria Martin is a 75-year-old female who presents for follow-up. She reports that she has been doing well, but her blood sugars are not well controlled. She received a letter from the clinic last time she was seen, and she has been taking the 2 mg glimepiride twice daily. She denies increasing her glimepiride dosage.

The patient reports that she has not been trying to eat healthier, as she does not like pasta and does not often have bread in the house. She states that she usually has 2 slices of wheat bread per day and occasionally has peanut butter sandwiches. She drinks club soda and seltzer water, but not regular water.

The patient reports that her eye exams are up-to-date, but she is not happy with her current lens. She had cataract surgery and is seeing improvement with her vision in one eye, but notes that the other eye is still blurry. The patient had iodine for her eyes.

The patient reports that her blood pressure was 116/60 mmHg two weeks ago. She is on a combination of medications for hypertension, including metoprolol 50 mg once daily, lisinopril/hydrochlorothiazide 20/25 mg once daily, and amlodipine 10 mg once daily. The patient denies taking all of these medications as prescribed.

The patient reports that she is tolerating atorvastatin well, but notes that her feet feel like hell due to peripheral neuropathy. She also experiences pain in her hips and upper legs.

The patient reports that she is still smoking cigarettes.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Cardiovascular: Denies headaches or dizziness.
• Respiratory: Reports coughing lately due to congestion; clear sputum; denies shortness of breath or coughing up blood; denies chest pain or pressure or tightness; denies nausea or vomiting; denies GI symptoms.
• Neurological: Reports decreased sensation in the tips of the first and second toes.
note.objective_exam:

• Cardiovascular: Carotids are normal in intensity and no murmurs heard at the auscultation area.

RESULTS

Hemoglobin A1C: 9.9%.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Type 2 diabetes mellitus.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient's hemoglobin A1C was elevated at 9.9%. Her blood pressure was elevated at 140/60 mmHg on two separate occasions. Her cholesterol level was elevated at this visit as well as on previous visits when labs were available.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed dietary modifications with the patient today including reducing carbohydrate intake and increasing fiber intake. We also discussed increasing her glimepiride dosage to 4 mg twice daily as previously recommended by clinic staff via letter. We also discussed continuing metformin as prescribed by clinic staff via letter today as well as continuing all prescribed medications for hypertension and hyperlipidemia including metoprolol 50 mg once daily, lisinopril/hydrochlorothiazide 20/25 mg once daily, amlodipine 10 mg once daily, atorvastatin high dose once daily, and smoking cessation again today.
- Medical Treatment: Continue metformin as prescribed by clinic staff via letter today; increase glimepiride dosage to 4 mg twice daily; continue all prescribed medications for hypertension and hyperlipidemia including metoprolol 50 mg once daily, lisinopril/hydrochlorothiazide 20/25 mg once daily, amlodipine 10 mg once daily, atorvastatin high dose once daily; refer for smoking cessation again today.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Evaluating right and left hand numbness and tingling.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Mr. Elijah Cook is a 60-year-old right-handed male who presents today for the evaluation of right and left hand numbness and tingling. The onset of his symptoms began 2 weeks ago, after he noticed that his symptoms were worse than they were at the time of his motor vehicle accident in December 2019. He sustained a broken wrist at the time of the accident, which was treated with a splint. He has been wearing the splint on both wrists, but he notes that his right wrist is worse than his left wrist. The patient reports that he has been experiencing mild stiffness in his neck as well, due to a contusion from the accident.

The patient describes his symptoms as bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome or potentially cubital tunnel syndrome. He notes that he experiences pain, soreness, and weakness in both hands, especially when using them. The pain is more pronounced at night and comes and goes throughout the day. He denies any loss of sensation in his hands or fingers, but notes that they may be less sensitive than they should be.

The patient reports that he has been taking nerve pain medicine for his symptoms, but has not been taking it regularly.

PAST HISTORY

The patient reports a history of hypertension for which he takes Coreg. He also reports a history of anxiety for which he takes Lexapro. He notes that he had prediabetes but was able to control it with dietary changes.

CURRENT MEDICATIONS

The patient reports that he is still taking Coreg for hypertension and Lexapro for anxiety.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Constitutional: Denies thyroid issues.
Gastrointestinal: Reports excessive appetite and bloating.
Eyes: Reports floaters.
Cardiovascular: Reports shortness of breath and leg swelling.
Endocrine: Reports always being hungry.
Skin: Reports nail bed changes, dryness, itching.
Musculoskeletal: Reports gout and muscle pain.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Neurological Examination:
Right Hand Examination:        Sensation is normal except pin prick sensation diminished in third and fourth fingers on the right side.    Reflexes are 1+ bilaterally; 2+ knees; toes are downgoing bilaterally.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS
Nerve conduction studies were performed today in office. These revealed evidence of bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
After reviewing the patient's examination today, I have had a lengthy discussion with him regarding his current symptoms. We discussed possible causes for his symptoms including bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome or potentially cubital tunnel syndrome due to past trauma to both wrists at the time of his motor vehicle accident in December 2019. We discussed treatment options including an EMG test to determine exactly where the nerve irritation is coming from. If this confirms bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome we will discuss possible treatment options including injections or carpal tunnel release surgery or referral to an orthopedist for similar treatment options.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Bilateral hand numbness and tingling.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Kimberly Taylor is a 60-year-old right-handed female who presents for the evaluation of bilateral hand numbness and tingling. The onset of her symptoms began 2 weeks ago, after she broke her wrists in a motor vehicle accident. She reports that she has noticed more tingling and numbness in her hands since then, but once they heal, the symptoms have been present. She notes that the right wrist is worse than the left. The patient reports that she wears a splint on both wrists, but only the left one sometimes. The splint seems to help with her symptoms.

The patient describes her symptoms as sore, with throbbing pain at times. She notes that when she is using her hands, they feel weaker. The tingling happens some more when she is using them, but when they hurt, it goes away and then the tingling is just dull.

The patient denies any loss of sensation in her hands or fingers. She states that they might be less sensitive than they should be, but she can still feel them. She was prescribed nerve pain medication which she has not been taking as directed.

The patient reports that her symptoms are worse at night and come and go throughout the day.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Constitutional: Reports fatigue and weight gain.
GI: Excessive appetite and bloating.
Eyes: Floaters.
Cardiovascular: Shortness of breath and leg swelling.
Endocrine: Positive diabetes, always hungry.
Skin: Nail bed trenches, dryness, itching.
Musculoskeletal: Gout, muscle pain.
Neurological: Parasthesia, bilateral hands.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Neurological Examination:
• Sensations normal except pin prick sensation diminished in the 3rd and 4th fingers on the right side and 4th and 5th fingers on the left side.
• Reflexes are 1+ bilaterally symmetric at knees; 2+ bilaterally down going toes.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS
No metastatic disease or acute intracranial abnormalities on CT brain with and without contrast performed on 02/05/2021.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome with question of bilateral cubital tunnel syndrome.
• Medical Reasoning: The patient's history of motor vehicle accident with broken wrists may have caused bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome or cubital tunnel syndrome. Her current symptoms are consistent with these diagnoses. We discussed this with the patient today in detail.
• Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed treatment options for carpal tunnel syndrome including EMG/NCV testing if necessary. If her symptoms do not resolve after testing we can consider hand clinic referral for possible symptomatic injections or carpal tunnel release surgery although she can pursue these through her current orthopedist. I encouraged her to wear splints as well as continue taking prescribed medications as directed by orthopedist.

1. GERD with possible functional etiology.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Acute to chronic constipation.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Michelle King is a 39-year-old female with a history of quadriplegia due to prior spinal cord injury. She was admitted to District Regional Hospital on 06/29/2021, and was discharged on 07/02/2021. The patient is currently being followed up for concerns regarding spasms, lightheadedness, significant constipation, and reported diaphoresis.

The patient was evaluated in the emergency department where she was febrile and had significantly elevated white blood cell count of 23,000. There were concerns for ongoing urinary tract infection, but she was treated with IV antibiotic therapy. She had labile blood pressure, headache, and vomiting. In the end, she slowly improved. She does have a supra-pubic catheter. Cultures were obtained and reviewed.

The patient presents today to follow up regarding these concerns.

The patient reports that she believes her hospitalization was more likely due to her dysreflexia from her quadriplegia that typically occurs. She did have a lot of vital signs changes including blood pressure fluctuations. The patient feels like she has a good bowel regimen including taking MiraLAX regularly as a primary treatment for constipation issues as well as lactulose for severe constipation. She feels like this was less likely a true urinary tract infection and was just related to her constipation however we did have a good discussion regarding her leukocytosis.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Constitutional: Denies fever.
• Cardiovascular: Reports hypertension.
• Gastrointestinal: Reports constipation.
• Musculoskeletal: Reports spasms.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Neurological: Examination of the nervous system is unremarkable.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Cultures were obtained and reviewed.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Acute to chronic constipation.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient believes that her hospitalization was more likely due to dysreflexia from her quadriplegia that typically occurs. She did have labile blood pressure fluctuations which could be related to this condition as well as significant constipation which may be contributing to the elevated white blood cell count.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed the possibility of dysreflexia in detail today and I explained that it can cause labile blood pressure fluctuations as well as significant abdominal pain which can lead to vomiting and diaphoresis. We also discussed the possibility of constipation being related to this condition as well as other factors such as dehydration which can exacerbate symptoms of dysreflexia.
- Medical Treatment: I recommended that we obtain updated fasting labs in 3 weeks or sooner if symptoms worsen or if there is any change in vital signs or symptoms at home. Repeat CBC will be ordered at that time to ensure white blood cell count has decreased.
Quadriplegia.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient has been followed up previously today regarding concerns regarding spasms, lightheadedness, significant constipation, and reported diaphoresis.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed the nature of quadriplegia in detail today including how it affects bowel function which can lead to constipation due to decreased sensation in the rectum.
- Medical Treatment: No treatment necessary at this time but we will follow up in 3 weeks or sooner if symptoms worsen or if there is any change in vital signs or symptoms at home.
Covid vaccine status.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient is unvaccinated against COVID-19 despite being high risk due to her quadriplegia status. We discussed the risks associated with COVID-19 including severe illness and death in individuals with underlying medical conditions such as quadriplegia who are unable to seek medical care when they become ill due to their limited mobility. We also discussed alternative treatments such as monoclonal antibodies which may not be effective for all patients with COVID-19 but may provide some benefit for those who are unable to receive vaccination due to their underlying medical condition.

Ashley James is a 14-year-old female who presents for evaluation of abnormal renal ultrasound with an atrophic right kidney. She was initially treated for a stomach virus, but her symptoms did not improve. She was then seen by another physician who performed an ultrasound and found that one of her kidneys was smaller than the other. The patient has been experiencing some stomach burning and dysuria, which she states is worse when she drinks certain beverages such as soda. She denies hematuria.

The patient's mother reports that Ashley has been experiencing some gastrointestinal symptoms since she was 4 years old, including vomiting and fever, which would last for several days at a time. The mother notes that the patient would have fevers and symptoms again several weeks later, but they would eventually resolve on their own.

The patient's maternal grandfather had posterior urethral valves and obstructive neuropathy, which led to end-stage chronic kidney disease and dialysis-dependent status. He underwent a renal transplant but it failed and he died at the age of 47 due to complications from dialysis.

PAST HISTORY

Pepcid 40 mg once daily.
Claritin as needed for allergies.

RESULTS

Abdominal Ultrasound, 03/22/2021.

CMP, 03/22/2021.
note.assessment_and_plan:

Ashley James is a 14-year-old female who presents for evaluation of abnormal renal ultrasound with an atrophic right kidney. Her current examination reveals no acute distress or abnormalities in respiratory or cardiovascular examination findings.

• Additional Testing: Annual ultrasound of kidneys, complete urinalysis, blood pressure check.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Left lower back pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Sean Phillips is a 35-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for evaluation of left lower back pain. The onset of his pain began in November 2020, when he underwent a lumbar microdiscectomy. He reports that he had severe nerve pain through his back and lower extremities prior to the surgery. He was prescribed high-dose gabapentin for this symptom.

The patient reports that his pain is worse with bending over, weight-bearing, and palpation to the left L5. He denies any pain with flexion or extension of his spine. He does report some right-sided pain on occasion, but it is generally located around the site of his previous surgery.

The patient denies any improvement with stretching, icing, or taking ibuprofen 800 mg daily. He notes that he was highly dosed up on gabapentin and it was difficult to withdraw from.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports left lower back pain.
Neurological: Reports left-sided nerve pain.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Neurological: Examination of the nervous system reveals normal sensation in the bilateral lower extremities. Motor strength is normal in all muscle groups.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS
X-ray images of the lumbar spine were obtained today and reveal no evidence of fracture or other abnormalities in the spine or vertebrae. Previous surgical site is visible and appears to have healed properly.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Left lower back strain.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient's history and physical examination reveal a left lower back strain. His x-rays from 11/2020 show no evidence of fracture or other abnormalities in the spine or vertebrae. Previous surgical site is visible and appears to have healed properly.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed treatment options with the patient today including physical therapy, meloxicam, demerol, and referral to pain management for further evaluation.
- Medical Treatment: We have started him on meloxicam for pain management. I also wrote a referral to pain management for further evaluation.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Sudden visual distortions and blurring of vision.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Mrs. White is a 77-year-old female who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of sudden visual distortions and blurring of vision. The onset of her symptoms began 2 weeks ago. She reports that she has been having trouble reading and straight lines, as well as noticing that her door frames have been looking crooked to her. She also reports that she has trouble adjusting to dim lights when going out to dinner with her husband.

The patient denies any history of macular degeneration.

PAST HISTORY

Patient reports that she smokes approximately 1 pack of cigarettes per day. She has tried to stop smoking on several occasions but has been unable to quit completely.

SOCIAL HISTORY

Patient reports that she is married and lives in Arlington, TX. She enjoys going out to dinner at McDonald’s, where she orders eggplant parmesan.

MEDICATIONS AND RECOMMENDATIONS IN USE

Patient reports that she takes blood pressure medication when she remembers to do so.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Visual: Reports sudden visual distortions and blurring of vision.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
• Eyes: Examination reveals posterior chamber intraocular lenses in both eyes. Right eye: Cornea is clear with no mVI cupping or PCIOL cup to disc is.2. Fundus examination shows the retina is attached 360 degrees without any tears or holes or pe changes in the fovea. Posterior segment exam shows drusen in the macula, thickening of the retina, presence of subretinal fluid and exudates accumulation positive for hemorrhage. Left eye: Cornea is clear with no mVI cupping or PCIOL cup to disc is.3 or pe changes in the fovea no hemorrhage or subretinal fluid retina is attached.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS
• Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT) shows drusen deposit, retinal pigment epithelium with subretinal fluid accumulation, choroidal neovascular membrane can be visualized.
• Fluorescein Angiography reveals focal areas of leakage in the right eye consistent with neovascular age-related macular degeneration.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
• Neovascular age-related macular degeneration.
• Medical Reasoning: The patient’s OCT results show drusen deposit, retinal pigment epithelium with subretinal fluid accumulation, choroidal neovascular membrane can be visualized. Fluorescein angiography reveals focal areas of leakage in the right eye consistent with neovascular age-related macular degeneration.
• Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed the nature of her diagnosis today and reviewed treatment options in detail. I explained that this is advanced disease that usually leads to more severe vision loss when those abnormal blood vessels start growing beneath the retina and they will leak fluid and blood which can create a large blind spot in the center of her visual field.
• Medical Treatment: I have prescribed Lucentis injections once a month into the vitreous portion of her eye after it has been numbed. Injections are given regularly over a period of time it may slow down the rate of vision decline or stop further vision loss but however this disease may also progress despite treatment.
• Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with recommended medical treatment plan.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Right ankle pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Jacqueline Price is a 28-year-old female who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of right ankle pain. The onset of her symptoms began 1 day ago when she was participating in a mountain biking lesson. She was riding as a messenger and fell off her bike, twisting her right ankle. She reports that her ankle twisted outward. The patient describes her pain as being located on the outer aspect of her ankle. She denies any numbness or tingling in her toes, but does report some numbness in other areas, including her heart. The patient is able to move her right ankle slightly, but is unable to bear weight on it. She is limping and reports that she has taken Tylenol for pain relief without any improvement.

The patient states that she heard a crack when she fell off the bike.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports right ankle pain and swelling.
Neurological: Reports numbness in other areas, including heart.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Vital signs are within normal limits.
Right ankle exam: There is some edema and erythema on the lateral malleolus on the right hand side. There is associated ecchymosis and a few excoriations. There is pain to palpation of the right lateral malleolus. Decreased flexion and extension of the right ankle as well as internal and external rotation.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

X-ray of the right foot obtained today, not yet reviewed.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

After reviewing the patient's examination today, I have had a lengthy discussion with her regarding her current symptoms.

The patient presents with an acute right ankle sprain without acute fracture or bony abnormality on radiographic examination today. We discussed treatment options at length today, including immobilization in an air cast, crutches for ambulation, meloxicam 15 mg once daily for pain control, ice 20 minutes 5 times daily for inflammation reduction, weight-bearing as tolerated, and follow-up in 2 weeks if no improvement.

INSTRUCTIONS: Follow up with me in 2 weeks if no improvement.
