CHIEF COMPLAINT

Right knee pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

The patient is a 33-year-old female who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of right knee pain. She reports that she fell off of a tandem bicycle and struck her right knee on a curb approximately 2 weeks ago. She localizes her pain to the medial aspect of the knee. She also reports occasional clicking with full extension of the knee, as well as occasional instability with ambulation. The patient states that her pain is the worst when ambulating up an incline. She denies any previous right knee issues. She enjoys walking her dogs and swimming but has not done this since her injury.

MEDICATIONS

The patient reports that she has been taking ibuprofen.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports right knee pain.
Neurological: Denies any neurological symptoms.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

MSK Examination: Examination of the right knee reveals medial joint line tenderness. Pes bursa is nontender, epicondyle is nontender, and back of her knee is nice and soft. Popliteal space is nontender on both sides. There are about a dime size little abrasions dry looks about a week old right over the medial patella. Everything else looks good with no scars present. Range of motion is full bilaterally without pain or stiffness.
Ligamentous Stability Testing: Right lateral collateral ligament intact, valgus stress test negative, Lachman test negative, anterior drawer negative.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

4 views of the right knee were obtained today and reviewed in office today.
These appear to be normal with no evidence of bone spurs or fractures present.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Right Knee Pain.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient sustained an injury to her posterior cruciate ligament (PCL) given her history and examination findings today.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed treatment options including bracing, physical therapy, and possible surgery if necessary at this point in time.
- Medical Treatment: Continue taking ibuprofen up to 3 times per day as needed for pain control. Ice packs 2-3 times per day to reduce swelling. We will also try a prescription for naproxen twice daily for 1 week to see if it helps with pain control without missing doses.
- Additional Testing: MRI of the right knee will be ordered for further evaluation.
- Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with the recommended medical treatment plan.

Left shoulder pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Betty Rogers is a 50-year-old female who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of left shoulder pain. The onset of her pain began 2 weeks ago. She denies any previous trauma or injury to her left shoulder. She is very active and has been renovating her basement recently. The patient reports that she has been doing a lot with that, but she does not remember hitting her shoulder or doing anything that would cause the pain. She states that she is active and will have aches and pains here and there, but nothing that some Tylenol cannot take care of.

The patient reports that her pain is isolated to her left shoulder. She states that she has limited mobility with reaching for things or lifting anything due to the pain. She also states that she cannot raise her arm over her head because it really hurts. The patient reports that she has constant pain, even when she sleeps on her side, but when she sleeps directly on it, the pain goes away.

The patient reports that she has been taking Tylenol Extra Strength 2 tablets every 6 to 8 hours as needed for pain relief. Without Tylenol, her pain level is a 3 out of 10, but with Tylenol, it goes down to a 2 or 3 out of 10.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports left shoulder pain.

Right knee pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Matthew Allen is a 40-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of right knee pain. The onset of his symptoms began yesterday when he was playing basketball. He states that he felt his knee pop and he started swelling and he could hardly walk after that. He denies any previous history of right knee pain.

The patient reports that his pain is located on the medial aspect of his right knee. He states that he is able to bear weight on his right leg, but he is favoring it for sure. He describes his pain as achy in nature. The patient reports that the swelling has decreased since he slept overnight. He denies any history of trauma to the right knee.

The patient reports that he has been taking Tylenol for pain, but it has not helped him very much. He notes that being off of Tylenol does help more than anything.

Regarding his hypertension, the patient reports that his blood pressure has been in the 140-150/80 range today. He notes that this is a little bit high, but he knows we discussed getting a blood pressure cuff at home and taking those so he does not check it very often.

The patient reports that he has been taking Norvasc 5 mg daily as prescribed by me.

Regarding his diabetes, the patient reports that his A1C was 7.2 which is not so good at this time. The patient reports that he has been taking Metformin 500 mg daily, but sometimes it causes gastrointestinal upset so he just skips it when it happens.

The patient denies any history of diabetes.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports right knee pain.
Cardiovascular: Denies chest pain or dyspnea on exertion.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Respiratory: Lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

X-ray of the right knee reveals no evidence of fractures or bony abnormalities.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Right Knee MCL Strain/MCL Tear.
- Medical Reasoning: The x-ray revealed no evidence of fractures or bony abnormalities, however, there was some swelling and ecchymosis present over the medial aspect of the right knee joint with negative varus and valgus testing which suggests a possible MCL strain or tear.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed treatment options with the patient today including continued use of Tylenol for pain management and prescription for Meloxicam 15 mg once daily for pain management and swelling reduction as well as placement in a knee immobilizer for 2 weeks to allow time for an MRI to be completed to confirm if there is a tear present or not.
- Medical Treatment: Continue with Tylenol as prescribed for pain management only until we receive results from MRI. Prescribed Meloxicam 15 mg once daily for pain management and swelling reduction as well as placement in a knee immobilizer for 2 weeks to allow time for an MRI to be completed to confirm if there is a tear present or not.
2. Hypertension.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient's blood pressure was elevated at today's visit with readings in the 140/80 range which is slightly elevated from normal values which should be around 120/80.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed treatment options with the patient today including increasing medication dosage from Norvasc 5 mg once daily to try to get blood pressure down into normal range values which should be around 120/80.
- Medical Treatment: Increase Norvasc dosage from 5 mg once daily up to 10 mg once daily.

He notes that he has been experiencing lightheadedness and slight headaches when his blood pressure is elevated. He denies any chest pain or respiratory symptoms. The patient also reports that he has experienced unsteadiness when he feels dizzy and a slight headache when his blood pressure numbers have been higher.

The patient states that he has not had any fever, nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. He denies palpitations or heart racing. He reports that he is still taking lisinopril 20 mg twice per day and notes that he rarely misses doses. The patient adds that he has used a pill box and then tried an app to help him keep track of his medication schedule, which was helpful but confusing at first.

The patient reports that he is still taking atorvastatin for his hyperlipidemia and notes that his osteoarthritis is controlled with Tylenol for mild pain when needed. He states that he is able to walk the full course of golf most of the time but will sometimes reduce his activity due to weather changes.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Cardiovascular: Reports lightheadedness, slight headaches, chest heaviness.
• Neurological: Reports unsteadiness when feeling dizzy.
• Respiratory: Denies respiratory symptoms.
• Gastrointestinal: Denies nausea, vomiting, diarrhea.
note.objective_exam:

- Medical Treatment: I am going to increase the lisinopril dose to 60 mg twice per day and add hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg per day which should help even out his blood pressure readings. I want him to check his blood pressure twice daily for the next two weeks then we will re-evaluate in two weeks.

- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed lifestyle modifications such as staying active but not overdoing it with golfing when possible with the patient today.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Theresa Rodriguez is a 41-year-old female who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of high blood pressure.

Medical Reasoning:
High blood pressure is a multifactorial condition that can be caused by diet, medication regimen, and other factors. The patient's current medication regimen consists of chlorthalidone, which may not be effective due to non-adherence with prescribed dosing schedule. The patient's diet is high in sodium from fast food consumption, which can contribute to elevated blood pressure levels.
In addition to these factors, the patient's diabetes may also be contributing to her elevated blood pressure levels as well as her elevated fasting glucose level today.
Patient Education and Counseling:
The patient will continue with her current medication regimen today but will work on adhering to the prescribed dosing schedule daily using reminders such as an iPhone reminder app.
We will also monitor her blood pressure three times per week at home using a home blood pressure monitor until we see improvement in her symptoms at which point we can decrease frequency of monitoring.
The patient will also work with a nutritionist to develop a low sodium diet plan in order to reduce sodium intake from fast food consumption.
The patient will increase her metformin dose to 1500 mg twice daily in order to improve glycemic control.

note.assessment_and_plan:

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Vision changes.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Matthew Thomas is a 65-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for evaluation of vision changes. The onset of his symptoms began approximately 3 to 4 months ago. He reports that he has trouble adjusting in dark environments, particularly when reading. He also notes that straight lines appear wavy to him, which he attributes to the paneling in his office. He denies any improvement in his symptoms.

The patient reports that he and his wife eat out almost every night and it is when they go to fancy places that he notices his vision changes. He states that he has tried hypnosis, lozenges, and chewing gum in an attempt to quit smoking but is unable to do so.

PAST HISTORY

The patient reports a history of high blood pressure.

SOCIAL HISTORY

The patient reports that he smokes 1 pack of cigarettes daily.

MEDICATIONS

The patient reports taking blood pressure medication as prescribed.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Constitutional: Denies weight loss or gain.
• Eye: Reports vision changes, difficulty adjusting in dark environments, straight lines appear wavy.
• Respiratory: Reports smoking history.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
• Ears, Nose, Mouth and Throat: Examination of the eyes reveals clear corneas bilaterally with no signs of nystagmus or strabismus. The anterior segment examination reveals posterior chamber intraocular lenses in both eyes. The cornea is clear bilaterally with no signs of nvi or peak hole cupping. Cup to disc ratio is 0.2 bilaterally. Fundus examination of the right eye shows the retina attached 360 degrees with no holes or tears noted and RPE changes in the fovea. There are drusen deposits under the RPE bilaterally with subretinal fluid accumulation and exudate accumulation present bilaterally. It is positive for hemorrhage in the right eye only.
• Neurological: Examination of the cranial nerves II-XII reveals no abnormalities.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS
• Diagnostic Exam: OCT exam shows drusen deposits under the RPE which is the retinal pigment epithelium and then subretinal fluid so SRF accumulation and choroidal neovascular membrane can also be visualized in that test.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
• Medical Reasoning: The diagnostic exam and eye exams are consistent with neovascular age-related macular degeneration (wet macular degeneration). This condition is characterized by abnormal blood vessels growing beneath the retina which leak fluid and blood leading to secondary complications such as large blind spots in the center of your visual field due to fluid leakage from these abnormal vessels into the subretinal space.
• Patient Education and Counseling: I have discussed treatment options with the patient today including injection therapy with Lucentis once per month which will help slow down disease progression but may not completely stop it at this point due to advanced disease stage at this point.
• Medical Treatment: We will schedule an injection today for treatment of neovascular age-related macular degeneration (wet macular degeneration).
• Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with recommended medical treatment plan.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Kidney stone.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Joshua Reyes is an 18-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of right flank pain. The onset of his pain began 2 weeks ago. The pain is intermittent and radiates down to his groin. He notes that his pain is usually controlled with ibuprofen, but he has had episodes where the pain radiates to his testicles. He denies any hematuria.

The patient reports that he has a history of kidney stones, which he has passed independently within a week, while others required surgical intervention or lithotripsy. He also notes that his family members have a history of kidney stones.

PAST HISTORY

Personal history of kidney stones, some passed independently, usually within a week, while others required surgical intervention or lithotripsy.
Significant family history of kidney stones.

SOCIAL HISTORY

Patient reports being an active individual.
Medications: Ibuprofen (over-the-counter).
Allergies: None reported.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

• Cardiovascular: Blood pressure is slightly elevated. No murmurs or gallops heard in auscultation of the heart. No extra heart sounds heard in auscultation of the lungs.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

CT scan of the right flank was reviewed today, 05/06/2022. It revealed a kidney stone measuring 0.5 cm in size, located on the proximal right ureter. There is no evidence of hydronephrosis.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Joshua Reyes is an 18-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of right flank pain.
• Medical Reasoning: The patient's CT scan revealed a kidney stone measuring 0.5 cm in size, located on the proximal right ureter with no evidence of hydronephrosis.
• Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed treatment options with him today and he understands what we discussed.
• Medical Treatment: Continue pushing fluids and hopefully we can pass the stone. Continue ibuprofen as needed for pain control. Prescribe tramadol 50 mg as needed for breakthrough pain if necessary due to increased discomfort over the weekend. Continue using strainer when urinating as recommended by PCP prior to seeing me today.
• Additional Testing: Order BMP, urinalysis and urine culture to evaluate for infection if present.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Shortness of breath.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Mr. Frank Lee is a 54-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of shortness of breath. He reports that he has been experiencing shortness of breath for approximately 1 week. He states that he has been watching his salt intake, but he believes that his diet has not been as good as it should have been during the holidays. He denies any swelling in his legs.

The patient reports that he was treated for shortness of breath 6 months ago and his Lasix dose was increased from 40 mg once a day to 40 mg twice a day and he seemed to get better. He denies any nocturia.

The patient reports that he is taking Lasix 40 mg once a day and denies any urination changes. He does report that he urinates at night, but this has not changed.

PAST HISTORY

Mr. Lee reports a history of coronary disease, acute myocardial infarction in 2018, placement of a coronary artery stent in the right coronary artery in 2018, and stage 3 chronic kidney disease.

CURRENT MEDICATIONS

Mr. Lee reports taking Lasix 40 mg once a day.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Denies pain in the lower extremities.
Cardiovascular: Denies chest pain.
Respiratory: Reports shortness of breath at rest and with exertion.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Neck: JVD up to 9 cm bilaterally present.
Lungs: Bibasilar crackles with occasional rhonchi clearing with coughing bilaterally present.
Heart: Grade 3/6 systolic ejection murmur heard at the left base present.
Lower Extremities: Pitting edema bilaterally present.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Chest X-ray ordered.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Acute heart failure exacerbation due to possible fluid overload secondary to dietary indiscretion.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient's history of coronary disease, acute myocardial infarction in 2018, placement of a coronary artery stent in the right coronary artery in 2018, and stage 3 chronic kidney disease are all relevant to this patient's current presentation. The patient's symptoms began after the holidays when his diet was less than optimal. His current medication regimen includes Lasix which is being increased from 40 mg once daily to 80 mg once daily due to worsening symptoms. We discussed dietary modifications with him today and I have ordered a referral for him to see a dietitian for further guidance on managing his sodium intake and weight loss plan.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed dietary modifications with him today including reducing sodium intake and increasing potassium intake through non-potassium rich foods such as fruits and vegetables. I also advised him on how to take his medication safely at home today.
- Medical Treatment: Increase Lasix from 40 mg once daily to 80 mg once daily starting tomorrow morning with an additional dose given at approximately 4 pm if necessary due to potential nocturia. Obtain chest x-ray due to possible pulmonary edema or other cardiac pathology.
